summary: Pipeline v0 runs end to end on real data but does not yet beat the one-prompt baseline.

stages.name: Prove the pipeline
stages.desc: CS and networking short answers: DigiKlausur, SAF, Mohler

stages.name: STEM with working
stages.desc: Maths, physics, chemistry; generated practice sheets, ProcessBench, PRM800K

stages.name: Other fields
stages.desc: Optional, only if a good dataset turns up

steps.name: Set up
steps.note: Project folders, config file, model client with Claude CLI and API backends, 26 tests.

steps.name: Load data
steps.note: DigiKlausur, SAF and Mohler downloaded and loaded into one format; dev/test split by question.

steps.name: Baseline
steps.note: One-prompt grader and metrics script. First number to beat, from 24 DigiKlausur answers.

steps.name: Marking scheme maker
steps.note: Schemes written once per question and self-tested. 8 of 8 passed on DigiKlausur dev.

steps.name: Grader and checks
steps.note: Built, but marks are too strict and the quote check breaks on garbled formulas.

steps.name: Feedback and its checker
steps.note: Feedback writer and judge are built. Judge has not been run yet.

steps.name: Readable report page
steps.note: Per-run report.html with equations, numbered reading order, score sum, teacher mark vs ours. Sample view: autograde view --name <run> --limit 10.

steps.name: Improvement loop
steps.note: Study the biggest misses, adjust prompts, rerun, keep what helps.

steps.name: Final held-out run
steps.note: Run once on test questions, then write the results table.

next.s: Looser matching for formulas; when it still fails, flag the point instead of removing all credit.

next.t: Make marking points core ideas, not copies of the model answer
next.s: One idea per point, each worth marks on its own; drop elaboration. Today one point bundles 3 to 4 facts, so a student with the main idea loses half.

next.t: Tell the grader the model answer is one example, not the only answer
next.s: Marks follow the question and the points; correct ideas missing from the model answer still count.

next.t: Measure sensitivity to the model answer
next.s: Regrade the same student answers against a paraphrased and a shortened model answer. Report how much the marks move. Automatic, no labels.

next.t: Show the grader how this teacher marks
next.s: Add 2 to 3 teacher-graded answers per question from the dataset's dev split. Then adjust bias if it is still strict.

next.t: Run the feedback judge and the wider test
next.s: Judge on dk_pipeline, then baseline vs pipeline on SAF and Mohler dev.

issues.t: Marks depend too much on the model answer
issues.s: Each marking point copies several facts from it, and partial credit needs all of them. Seen in Q6 (SVM) and Q10 (backpropagation).

issues.t: Pipeline does not beat baseline yet
issues.s: Correlation 0.67 vs 0.78 on 24 answers. Small sample, so the gap may be noise, but it is not an improvement.
One 2/2 answer made of formulas was marked 0 after the retry also failed to quote exactly.

issues.t: Cost is about 5 times the baseline
issues.s: $0.70 vs $0.14 per 24 answers at list price. Scheme tests are paid once; marking plus feedback are two calls per answer.
No API key yet. The Claude CLI backend is the only one exercised.

issues.t: Teacher marks are lenient on DigiKlausur
issues.s: Most answers got full marks, so a strict grader looks worse. Check SAF and Mohler before tuning to this one.
A different project called autograde exists on PyPI. Only matters if we publish.

decisions.t: Fully automatic, no human step at run time
Plain Python, no LangGraph for now
Output format: file per student or table

compare.title: DigiKlausur, dev split, 24 answers, Claude Sonnet via CLI
compare.note: Single run on a small sample. Treat differences as hints until we measure run-to-run noise. Feedback quality has not been scored yet.
